title: Reference is a link
use: Explicit [caption](url) for anything tappable; a proposal links its subject before the reasoning.
boundary: Bare paths drop on mobile and in copies; every file on a branch gets its 🥏, a document included, and where no link reaches a change, say so (the honesty gate).

title: A screenshot
use: For a visual change, render the page headless with npm run shot and send the PNG, which a file card shows inline.
boundary: A viewport shot cannot show horizontal overflow; --measure checks it at phone width (the snag screenshot-hides-overflow).

title: A file card
use: SendUserFile attaches a file as a file card; a rendered link is usually preferred, and the download suits an uncommitted file or one opened in another application.
boundary: Images render inline; other types download to the device.

title: A rendered view
use: Render a file through the shared toss renderer rather than handing over source alone: npm run showing prints the link for a changed file, and --path for any file.
boundary: Private repos need the GitHub token, which is stored per browser.

title: Content in the link
use: Carry the content in the address: toss-render.html#gz= renders a page, and the app's #gz= carries text files, which npm run -s stage-link mints.
boundary: Needs no commit or token; the link's length limits the size.

title: Branch anchor
use: The first file-modifying reply leads with Working branch: [branch-name](url).

title: Open the branch
use: Link the live branch page beside the guide PR; its facts are read from the API on every load, so the link is current whenever opened. &pane= opens a pane and &file= opens the file deck on one path.
boundary: Token-gated with the in-app-browser caveat; 🌿 is where you read the branch, 🧭 where you merge it.

title: Guide pointer
use: Mark the branch's guide PR; close a reply with 🧭 [PR #N](url) (body synced | body not synced).
boundary: The parenthetical claims this reply rewrote the guide region, never carried forward.

title: Surfacing caption
use: End every reply with the 💬 session-page link; a file-modifying turn adds the file count and the turn commit, not a file list; the page enumerates.
boundary: The caption replaces a per-file list of [new]/[main]/[diff] links, never the prose. With no session record, the 🌿 branch link stands in.

title: Close in one order
use: Every reply ends the same way, parts skipped where they do not apply: the 💬 caption line, the render line, 🧭, then exactly one closing state, last.
boundary: The order never varies and nothing follows the state; a reply that changed no files still closes with one, but a wake that leaves the reader nothing new gets no reply, and if the harness then demands visible output, reply with one line naming the wake.

title: Closing state
use: Every reply that finishes work, proposes work, or leaves something open ends with exactly one of eleven states (🟢 ready to continue, ❇️ ready to assess, 🟡 pending, 🪧 direction needed, ✴️ needs you, 🟠 attention, ⚪ clean exit, 🟣 merged, 🔴 closed, ⚫ done, 🔵 short answer), or ⚖️ choice needed when presenting a call, so the next move is cheap to recognize.
boundary: Exactly one state per reply; the colour says who acts, so a green state is the session's work and 🟢 never instructs the reader while orange needs the reader (🪧 to set direction, ✴️ to do); go authorizes only what the 🟢 or ❇️ list names; uncertainty the session can investigate is ❇️ rather than 🪧 or ✴️, and ⚖️ presents a call, a decision only the reader can make, after a full assessment; every ✴️ ask ships the link that performs it, or says why none can exist; 🔵 puts the question itself in the bold lead; 🟣 and 🔴 mark the branch, not a task; attention debt gates green, so work that leaves the reader something to return to is ❇️ and names what it leaves; ⚪ is before the merge, 🟣 one merge, ⚫ after the last, and ⚫ is the only state about the session rather than the reply.

title: Subscribe the workstream PR
use: Call subscribe_pr_activity on creating a workstream PR. Subscribe once, receive every event, act per event: a go: comment instructs (intent, never authority), everything else is incoming context and obliges nothing.
boundary: Never schedule a check-in; the plugin refuses send_later, and create_trigger stays open for a reminder actually asked for. A PR event is news only as a failing check that is this session's work, a comment or review, an unreported merge or close, or a passing check the reader said to wait for.
